figures.caption: Table 1: Conceptual distinctions between reproducibility, replicability, robustness, and generalizability in data analysis pipelines. Adapted from the framework introduced by Nichols et al. (2022) and reproduced from the original publication in NeuroImage [3].

Figure 1: Overview of the BIDS-EEG data organization and associated metadata files. Schematic illustration of a Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) compliant EEG dataset, showing the directory hierarchy and the linkage between raw EEG recordings and their accompanying metadata. Adapted from Pernet et al. (2019), Scientific Data, under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License.

Figure 2: Brainstorm database organization illustrated using the PracticalMEEG dataset. Left: One-step automatic import interface for MEG-BIDS datasets in Brainstorm. Center: Subjectspecific anatomical files, including MRI volumes and reconstructed cortical surfaces. Right: Organized MEG/EEG recordings and associated preprocessing and analysis results within the Brainstorm database structure.

Figure 3: Brainstorm Plugin Manager as an Interoperability Hub. Brainstorm integrates with a broad ecosystem of neuroimaging tools (e.g., SPM, FieldTrip, OpenMEEG, BrainSuite, CAT, and others) through its plugin manager, enabling interoperable workflows, standardized data exchange, and reproducible analysis pipelines.

Figure 4: Example EEGLAB graphical user interface and visualization outputs. Screenshots show dataset information, an ERP image plot, scalp topography, and scrolling channel data, illustrating EEG visualization and preprocessing in EEGLAB.

Figure 5: Example EEGLAB script for importing and preprocessing an EEG-BIDS dataset. The workflow includes BIDS import, channel cleaning, filtering, re-referencing, independent component analysis (ICA), automated component labeling (ICLabel), artifact rejection, epoch extraction, and computation of single-trial measures within an EEGLAB STUDY structure. The full version of this script is available in the LIMO-EEG repository.

Figure 6: FieldTrip scripting workflow and data inspection interface. Left: An example of a MATLAB script implementing FieldTrip preprocessing steps (trial definition, filtering, and baseline correction). Right: The interactive data browser for visualizing trials and identifying artifacts.

Table 2: Overview of EEG analysis, acquisition, and processing software ecosystems. Representative tools are organized by functional domain, highlighting the diversity of tools supporting reproducible EEG research workflows.
